{{Short description|German mathematician (1931–2017)}}
{{about||the American flying ace|Walter G. Benz Jr.}}
[[File:Walter Benz.jpeg|thumb|Walter Benz in 1975<br>(photo from the [[Oberwolfach Research Institute for Mathematics]])]]
'''Walter Benz''' (May 2, 1931 [[Lahnstein]] – January 13, 2017 [[Ratzeburg]]) was a German [[mathematician]], an expert in [[geometry]].<ref>[http://lebenswege.faz.net/traueranzeige/walter-benz/48997763 Walter Benz : Traueranzeige] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191215081538/http://lebenswege.faz.net/traueranzeige/walter-benz/48997763 |date=2019-12-15 }} {{in lang|de}}</ref>

Benz studied at the [[Johannes Gutenberg University of Mainz]] and received his [[doctoral degree]] in 1954, with Robert Furch as his advisor.<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=21533}}</ref>
After a position at the [[Johann Wolfgang Goethe University Frankfurt am Main]], he served as a professor at [[Ruhr University Bochum]], [[University of Waterloo]], and [[University of Hamburg]]. Benz was honoured with the degree of a [[Honorary degree|Dr. h.c.]]

Based on his book ''Vorlesungen über Geometrie der Algebren'' ([[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]] 1973), certain geometric objects are called [[Benz plane]]s.

[[Inner product space]]s over the [[real number]]s provide the basis of a 2007 book by Benz: ''Classical Geometries in Modern Contexts''.<ref>W. Benz (2007) ''Classical Geometries in Modern Contexts: Geometry of Real Inner Product Spaces'', [[Birkhäuser]],
 {{ISBN|978-3-7643-8541-5}}</ref>
